questions.q: In standard traffic light signals, the **amber (yellow)** light instructs a motorist to...
options: accelerate quickly to clear the intersection.
slow down and prepare to stop unless it is unsafe to do so.
proceed immediately at maximum speed limit.
reverse the vehicle away from the intersection.
questions.explain:
Traffic light signals have standard universal indications:

| Light Colour | Directive to Driver |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Red** | Stop completely before the stop line |
| **Amber (Yellow)** | Slow down and prepare to stop (or clear if already in intersection) |
| **Green** | Proceed / Go if the way is clear |

questions.q: The primary purpose of enforcing traffic regulations on public roads is to...
options: maximize revenue generated through traffic fines and penalties.
prevent road traffic accidents, save lives, and maintain orderly movement.
discourage citizens from purchasing and driving private motor vehicles.
restrict commercial passenger vehicles to rural highways only.
questions.explain: Traffic regulations are rules enacted to control vehicular and pedestrian movement. Their main objective is to **minimize road accidents, protect lives and properties, and prevent vehicular congestion**.

questions.q: The statutory federal agency established in Nigeria to maintain safety, enforce traffic regulations, and reduce road crashes on federal highways is the...
options: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).
questions.explain: The **Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)** was established in 1988 as the lead government agency responsible for road safety administration, driver licensing, and traffic law enforcement on Nigerian highways.

questions.q: To ensure personal safety when crossing a busy urban roadway where there is no pedestrian flyover, pedestrians are legally advised to use the...
questions.explain: A **zebra crossing** consists of prominent black and white stripes painted across the road. By traffic law, approaching motorists must yield the right of way to pedestrians crossing on designated zebra crossings.
